Hi Whiteout, IF,

I've read thru the compression book and the video several times and I'm still not grasping the difference between compression and a flag.

In the video the definition of compression is taking out the last decision point and its orders. That I understand and can follow on the chart taking out each supply/demand area and seeing what has been consumed and what hasn't.

Where I'm stuck is between a flag and compression as a flag to me indicates price may continue to the price projection from the flag.

Maybe I'm harping on this needlessly but to me until I can understand it fully I'm always going to be unsure and have doubts about what I'm seeing.

If I spot a bull flag (and by that I mean a defined rectangle but skewed on an angle) then I do the measuring thing with the pole and extend it out from the break to get an idea of how far price will move. If this occurs just before a supply area and indicates that price may move deep or thru the supply then I am very wary about going short.

If I see price narrowing into a wedge/funnel type shape then I figure that is compression and I am happy to trade from the appropriate level.

When I watch LF's video to me I'm seeing a flag (rectangle skewed on an angle) where he is saying its compression into the start of the supply zone. To me I would be hesitant to go short even tho price is moving into daily supply as by the flag price projection it could almost all the way into the zone.

When watching the video fast forward to 6 min 30 sec and watch from there and the area I have as a flag is referred to as compression.

I have also attached a chart showing the H4 chart with what I see as compression and what I see as a flag pattern.

I feel a bit silly for not being able to understand the difference and appreciate your patience while I grasp the concept.

I hope I have explainded things clearly enough.

Yes, I don't have any stats on it either but was just going off what I've seen in general about price projections from different patterns.

When I saw how this site was laid out I made a mental note to just go thru things one step at a time. Over the past few days I've really focused on looking for CP in every chart and time frame I pull up. As with all things our ability to judge the context of situation will assist our outcomes.

I'm glad I just focused on this one thing as I feel I have a much better understanding of it now so a big thanks to Whiteout and If and all those associated with getting this site up and running.

Now that I revisit this example I think the overriding thing was a) understanding what was going on inside the flag which is compression and what it's effects are b) knowing where and how strong the supply zone is c) understanding the context of the situation to trade in direction which has the most probable outcome.
